questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Kenya about 581,309 square kilometres; Zimbabwe about 390,757 square kilometres; Uganda about 241,038 square kilometres; Seychelles about 459 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Kenya?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Kenya on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kenya article.

questions.proof: To the north, it borders Ethiopia; to the northwest, it borders South Sudan; to the south, Tanzania; and to the west, Uganda and Lake Victoria.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Kenya?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kenya article.

questions.proof: Its capital city is Nairobi, which is the 14th largest city in Africa (after Accra, Ghana).

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Kenya on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Kenya on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Nairobi?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Kenya is Nairobi.
